questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head.
questions.explanation: When making a turn, look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: Which is a poor reason to sound your horn?

options.text: A driver in the next lane is too close to the vehicle ahead.
A parked car has someone in the driver's seat.
You want people to look at your motorcycle.
You are passing a pedestrian in the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: You want people to look at your motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to alert drivers or pedestrians who may move into your lane. Sound your horn if a driver is too close to the vehicle ahead, if someone is in a parked car, or if you see a pedestrian or bicyclist in the street. Do not use your horn just to get attention.

questions.question: In a group ride, inexperienced riders should position themselves:

options.text: In the front of the group.
Close to the back of the group.
At the very end of the group.

questions.correctAnswerText: Just behind the leader.
questions.explanation: Less experienced riders should ride just behind the leader. This prevents them from falling behind the group. It also allows experienced riders behind them to watch and help if needed.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Always stay in the same part of your lane.
Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
Always ride in the center of the lane so other vehicles see you.
Ride in a zigzag pattern so drivers notice you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change your lane position as road and traffic conditions change.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best or should always be avoided. Adjust your position based on changing road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: When a vehicle is passing you from behind, you should:

options.text: Use the left portion of your lane.
Use the center portion of your lane.
Use the right portion of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use the center portion of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed, use the center portion of your lane. This is the safest position. Riding on the side closest to the passing vehicle increases your risk of collision. Riding on the far side may cause the other driver to cut back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: On a three-wheeled motorcycle or with a sidecar, do not ride too far to the right because:

options.text: Other drivers may not see you.
You will not pass other vehicles as easily.
Other drivers may try to share your lane.
You may run off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may run off the road.
questions.explanation: A sidecar extends to the right side of a motorcycle. The rear right wheel on a three-wheeled motorcycle sits far to the right. Riding too far right risks the sidecar or rear wheel leaving the road.

questions.question: When riding in a group, you should:

options.text: Place inexperienced riders at the back.
Not ride too close to other riders.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not ride too close to other riders.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation and check your mirrors regularly. Choose experienced riders as leaders and sweep riders. Keep proper distance between riders to stay safe.

questions.question: As your motorcycle's weight shifts forward while braking, you:

options.text: Can apply the front brake harder.
Should use less pressure on the front brake.
Can apply the rear brake harder.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can apply the front brake harder.
questions.explanation: As your weight shifts forward while braking, more traction becomes available to the front wheel. This means you can apply the front brake with more pressure.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.correctAnswerText: Warning
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers about upcoming road conditions and hazards.

questions.question: As weight shifts forward while you are braking, you should:

options.text: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
Not worry. Weight transfer will not affect your motorcycle.
Try to lock the front tire.

questions.correctAnswerText: Gradually increase pressure on the front brake.
questions.explanation: While braking, gradually increase the pressure on the front brake lever as the motorcycle's weight transfers forward to the front tire.

questions.question: Who should set the pace in a group of riders?

options.text: The riders just behind the leader

questions.correctAnswerText: The rider in back
questions.explanation: The last rider in a group should set the pace. This makes sure no riders are left behind.

questions.question: If you cannot avoid hitting an object in the road, you should:
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down before contact.
questions.explanation: If you cannot avoid hitting an object, slow down as much as you can. Keep your motorcycle upright, rise slightly off the seat, and roll the throttle slightly before impact.

questions.question: When riding in curves, turning, or entering a highway, the best group formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file.
questions.explanation: Use single-file formation when riding through curves, making turns, or entering or exiting a highway. Staggered formation is best for other group riding.

questions.question: In hot weather, wearing a riding jacket:

options.text: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
Is discouraged because it can cause heat-related problems.
Should only be done if the jacket is a light color.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can help protect against heat exhaustion and dehydration.
questions.explanation: Wear a riding jacket and long pants in hot weather. They protect you from crashes and also help prevent heat exhaustion and dehydration.

questions.question: When applying the front brake, you should:

options.text: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
Grab at the brake with only two fingers.
Press down on the brake lever with your foot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Apply the lever by squeezing firmly and progressively.
questions.explanation: Squeeze the brake lever firmly and smoothly with all four fingers. Apply more pressure gradually.

questions.question: Studies show that nearly ______ of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking.
questions.correctAnswerText: 40 percent
questions.explanation: About 40 percent of riders killed in motorcycle crashes had been drinking. Alcohol is a major cause of fatal motorcycle crashes.

questions.question: When exiting a highway while riding in a group, which formation should be used?
questions.correctAnswerText: Single-file
questions.explanation: Switch to single-file formation when exiting a highway. Use staggered formation for most group riding.

questions.question: Riding on the far side of a lane when following another vehicle:

options.text: Is recommended because you will be seen easily.
Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
Is recommended because a passenger in the vehicle may tell the driver that you are there.
Is illegal because you have to ride in the center portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is not recommended because drivers seldom use their side mirrors and may not see you.
questions.explanation: Most drivers check their rearview mirror more than their side mirrors. Ride in the center of the lane so the driver can see you in the rearview mirror.

questions.question: If a dog chases your motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Stop until the dog loses interest.
Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach the dog slowly, then speed up.
questions.explanation: Slow down and approach the dog. Then speed up and leave it behind. If a larger animal chases you, brake and prepare to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following will help you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.correctAnswerText: Using both brakes
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, reduce speed and use both brakes. Avoid sudden moves. Stay out of the center lane and follow tire tracks left by other vehicles. Watch for hazards like oil and gravel.

questions.question: A helmet should NOT:

options.text: Have been worn in a crash.

questions.correctAnswerText: Have been worn in a crash.
questions.explanation: The best helmet meets U.S. DOT standards, fits snugly, and has no obvious defects. If a helmet was worn during a crash, replace it.

questions.question: When a vehicle passes you on your left, you should:

options.text: Move as far right as possible.
Ride in the center of your lane.
Ride on the left side of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding near the passing vehicle increases crash risk. Riding far from it may cause them to merge back too soon. Stay centered.

questions.question: When being passed from behind, you should:

options.text: Stay on the left side of your lane.
Stay in the center of your lane.
Stay on the right side of your lane.
Make eye contact with the driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed from behind. Riding on either side is unsafe. The near side increases crash risk. The far side may cause them to return too soon.

questions.question: When riding in a group, the best formation is:
questions.correctAnswerText: A staggered formation.
questions.explanation: Use a staggered formation when riding in a group. Switch to single-file when turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving highways.

questions.question: How many paths of travel does each traffic lane offer a motorcyclist?
questions.correctAnswerText: Three
questions.explanation: Each traffic lane offers three paths: the left side, center, and right side of the lane.
